Comments: On 04/04/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 Well Site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). On 03/11/2024, the violations were issued as outstanding (IR 3726997). The operator was in compliance with schedule on 03/27/2024 (IR 3736262).The following was observed during inspection on 04/04/2024:Inspection conducted after several large rain events. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/17/2026 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga county. 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/17/2026
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 8281952
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/17/2026
Comments: On 7/17/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection was conducted in response to notification from Seneca of the installation of a concrete catch basin and corrugated pipe on the north side of the pad to capture surface waters on the pad. It was 70 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. I was unaccompanied during the inspection. When I arrived on site, I observed a trench that had recently been dug along the north side of the pad, the trench leading to a 4' x 2' x 2' deep cement catch basin as seen in pictures 12, 13, and 14. I did observe liquid in the trench that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS5 meter. The upper limit of the meter for conductivity is 19.99 mS. The liquid was flowing into the cement catch basin. A vac truck was staged on site with hose ends located in the catch basin, able to remove the accumulating liquids. The fluids were being transferred to a frac tank that had been staged near the catch basin. I inspected the bottom of the center rock lined outfall on the north side of the pad where it leads into the sediment basin. I did not observe liquids discharging from the pad into the basin during this inspection. Liquid in the sediment basin near the northeast overflow field tested at 9.01 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551266 from the sediment basin near the northeast overflow.13 wells have been completed at the site and were staged for flow-back/production. Sand separators and three-phase separators were installed on each of eight recently completed wellheads. The three-phase separators were being used to separate water, gas, and oil. The rig/frac operations secondary containment structure remains installed around the well heads, the sand separators and the three-phase units. Two produced water tanks and 13 GPUs were stationed in secondary containment. Nine frac tanks have been installed in secondary containment south of the eight new gas wells, these being used for flow-back. 32 frac tanks used during fracking operations remain stationed in secondary containment on the west side of the pad.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1030 hours.

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Inspection Date: 2/08/2021
Comments: At the time of inspection, well appears to be equipped for production (Photo 1). Well label and tag present on well head (Photo 2). Pipe extending from brine tank appears to have a leak. The pipe appears to have significant rusting. The soil underneath the elbow joint of the pipe is saturated (Photos 3 and 4). Photo 5 show the underside of the pipe as it appears wet. The Department observed liquid dripping from the area shown. Two conductivity readings were taken from the saturated soil (Photos 6 and 7) showing readings of 6,410 microsiemens and 14,840 microsiemens. No background readings of the soil were recorded due to the ground being frozen everywhere excluding the affected area, however, due to the elevated readings of the affected area it appears that release is occurring. Photo 8 shows brine tank with well label present. Photo 9 shows the top of the brine tank lacking third-party protection. The Department recommends that the spill be remediated. The Department recommends the pipe be remediated or replaced. The Department recommends that the brine tank is protected against third-party acts. The Department requests inspection logs for the brine tank for the past 3 months. The Department requests information on how much fluid was lost and how the operator quantifies that information. The Department requests the waste manifest once it is available. The Department contacted both Lisa Raffle and Josh Martz of Diversified and notified them of the leak; they said someone would be out to remediate as soon as possible.

A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/02/2026 to SCORPIO ENERGY INC in Howe Township, Forest county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SCORPIO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/02/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8287771
Permit API: 053-31161
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/02/2026
Comments: This site is undergoing construction for the development of a conventional well. The drilling permit and E and S Plan are posted at the entrance of the location. There was no activity on the location at the time of this inspection. The template for the site and access road has been completed. The gathering lines for this well have been buried within the template of the road. Stone has not yet been applied to any portion of the road or well site. The E and S Plan that was prepared for this site is inadequate as it does not account for all surface waters of the Commonwealth that converge with the earth disturbance associated with the construction of this well site and the access road that leads to it. In addition, the site and access road have been excavated significantly below the natural grade, therefore, watercourses that were likely below the surface prior to construction are now present at the surface and are not accounted for in the E and S Plan. Due to the insufficient plan and construction practices, the BMPs that have been installed are insufficient and are promoting stormwater to become concentrated and directed into waters of the Commonwealth. Numerous waters of the Commonwealth are also being removed from their natural channel and redirected.The ditches along the access road do not consist of a durable material, nor have they been stabilized to account for the flow of water running through them and have become significantly eroded due to the volume and velocity of stormwater and surface water. Aside from the lack of stabilization measures in the ditch, the roadside banks and perimeter of the location (that do not appear to require any additional excavation) have also not yet been stabilized. No perimeter BMPs (such as silt sock) have been installed for minimizing the amount of sediment leaving the un-stabilized areas of earth disturbance. The culverts that have been installed at the intermittent streams have been poorly installed. There is excessive excavation at the inlets and outlets of these water features resulting in sediment entering the stream channels. The E and S Plan does not account for headwall protection at these culverts, therefore, the disturbed earth near the inlets and outlets is vulnerable to scouring and erosion into the water channel. Improper installation and the lack of energy dissipators at the outlets of the installed cross-pipes that are conveying stormwater is resulting in scouring at the outlets of these culverts and increasing the amount of accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Since no stone has been placed on the road, recent traffic on the road template after rain events has caused the template to become soft and appreciably rutted in spots. This has allowed stormwater, and in some areas, the flow from a watercourse to flow onto the road template. As a result of these deficiencies, there has been accelerated erosion across the earth disturbance associated with the construction of the access road and well site. Significant amounts of sediment have discharged into and remain accumulated in spring seeps and unnamed tributary of Hastings Run.In addition to the E and S deficiencies, due to the abundance of shallow ground water at the site, the use of pits for temporary containment or permanent encapsulation of cuttings or any residual waste from this well in a pit would not satisfy the requirements outlined in Chapter 78.56(a)(8), unless Scorpio Energy can demonstrate otherwise to the Department in advance of lining the pit.The deficiencies noted above also apply to the first well location (Well Site 56) and the access road getting to that site. Corrective action should be applied to both sites in order to remediate the noted violations and to return to compliance.

Specialized Professional Services Inc. No staining is observed on the well pad at this time and there is no observable sheen on the fluid inside the secondary containment. Range Resources reportedly remediated the site in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1).Violations for the release are being issued and immediately corrected. The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.

Comments: On October 3 2025, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Nelson 2 OG Well in Dunbar Township, Fayette County in regard to violations issued under IR 3888353.At the time of the inspection, the well appeared to be equipped for production. The well posting was present at the time of the inspection. The access road appeared stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth.The previously observed release from the well head appeared to be active at the time of this inspection. The Department observed fluid actively dripping from the well head onto the gravel beneath it. While the previously observed orange-stained gravel around the well appeared to be visually remediated, a fluid leak still appeared to be active. A background soil conductivity reading was 0.05mS. A conductivity reading was taken of the fluid leaking from the well head with a reading of 4.11mS. A conductivity reading of fluid that has accumulated within the well casing was OR (over detectable range, >20.00mS).The Department previously requested the Operator evaluate the releases that have occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. No response has been received, therefore the Department is again requesting the aforementioned information.Based on today's inspection, violations remain outstanding for the observed release onsite.

Comments: The DEP conducted a routine inspection of Repsol's Twin Ridge 02-185 well site located in Covington Township, Tioga County on 5/18/2021 at 1400 hours. The weather was 77 degrees with mostly clear skies. The act 9 sign was observed at the entrance to the site. There are ten active wells on location. A crew was onsite today removing separators from the wells. The majority of the site remains permanently stabilized through vegetated cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed during today's inspection. Two frac tanks remain onsite and are held within secondary containment. Containment structures are intact and no leaks or other issues were identified. Pooled water on the pad surface was field measured and found to be low in electrical conductivity. There was no evidence of spills/releases observed onsite. Last year, the operator removed the sub base of the pad which consisted of cement and soil. The pad was then regraded and material replaced. A portion of the pad surface has been revegetated. Since construction has finished, the operator continues to monitor the stormwater collected in the basins. They plan on doing additional sampling sometime in June. Today, the basin located to the west was empty and the bottom was lacking in vegetation. The basin located to the south was retaining some water today. Silt sock remains in place below the basins and slopes to prevent water from escaping the site. Violations against API # 117-21997 cited on 6/24/2019 remain outstanding at this site from the previous release. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has been confirmed. No additional violations are cited at this time. I departed the site at 1440 hours.

Comments: On November 18, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a incident response inspection at the EQT ARO LLC Elbow Fish and Game Club Pad C. On November 16, 2024, Rick Hall with EQT notified the DEP spill hotline, it was reported that a line from a water truck failed. DEP spoke with Rick Hall on the phone and he informed DEP that a seal on a lubricator for a swabbing rig failed and sprayed about 5 gallons of produced fluid onto the well pad surface. The sprayed production fluid impacted an area of approximately 41 ft. by 18 ft. EQT had contractors onsite excavate the impacted soil and put it in a dumpster. When DEP arrived, the area of excavation had been backfilled with clean fill. There were no areas of staining or pooled watered near by. No E and S issues were observed during the time of inspection. The site appeared to be stable and well vegetated meeting the 70% uniform perennial vegetative cover.There are a total of 7 wells capable of producing located on this well pad. The wells have separators in line with them. All wells are tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the well cellars was observed. There are 7 GPUs and 4 steel vertical production fluids tanks onsite. Both the GPUs and production fluid tanks are stationed in secondary containment. One dehydration unit is located onsite in containment.Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted but the violations were immediately corrected.

Comments: On August 26, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Janoscrat 1 well in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection CEI inspection in response to violations issued under inspection 3400883 where violations were issued due to a possible brine discharge that was discovered on July 29, 2022. The following was observed:The brine tank from where the possible discharge occurred in inspection 3400883 has since been removed, and the area has been mulched and seeded (see photos 1 and 2). The hissing sound and gas odor previously noted on the well head in inspections 3400883 and 3399998 is no longer present (see photo 4). Newly updated operator's information has also been added (see photo 3). Soil conductivity readings were taken on both sides of what once appeared to be the brine puddle. The one taken on the side closest to the well at the former location of the brine tank read, .49 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken on the side farthest away from the well read .44 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. (See attached e-mail from Operator for depths of CET deployments). This is the 2nd post CET deployment SPBUTs being performed on these wells. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line.
